climate.overview_html: COP31 in Antalya moves into its political week. UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators to move faster to the hardest issues, and Chris Bowen expects a first draft of the deal this week. Finance and the just transition mechanism remain the main sticking points.

items.headline: Stiell urges COP31 negotiators to speed up as talks enter their second week
items.summary: Stiell asked delegations to avoid tactical delays as ministers arrive, while major producers resist firm targets on oil, gas and coal. Negotiations president Chris Bowen said a first draft agreement should appear this week; Swiss envoy Felix Wertli expects a tough second week.

major_events.name: Bay of Bengal depression (Akvan), India
major_events.impact: IMD upgraded the low to a depression on Nov 15 and expects a cyclonic storm on Nov 16 and a severe cyclonic storm on Nov 17, to be named Akvan. A live season summary cites an IMD outlook for landfall over Andhra Pradesh around Nov 19. Fishermen are told to stay ashore until Nov 20.

major_events.name: St. Johns River flooding, Florida
major_events.status: Major flood at Cocoa; crest 17.1 ft
major_events.impact: NWS Melbourne reports major flooding near Cocoa with a 17.1 ft crest forecast and water entering homes around Lake Poinsett. Downstream lakes in Seminole County are still expected to crest around Nov 20-23.

major_events.name: Nueces River flooding, Texas
major_events.impact: NWS Corpus Christi raised its Nueces River warning to moderate lowland flooding, with a crest near 15.9-16.2 ft and the warning running to Nov 18. Oil-field tanks, pumps and hunting cabins are affected.

major_events.name: Severe storms, eastern Australia
major_events.impact: BoM flagged likely severe thunderstorms across eastern Australia on Nov 15 and 16.

weather.overview_html: The Bay of Bengal system became a depression on Nov 15 and IMD expects it to become Cyclone Akvan today, with an Andhra Pradesh landfall possible around Nov 19. In the US, river flooding continues on the St. Johns and Nueces. NASA says Pacific sea-level data put the 2026 El Niño on track to rival 1997-98.

items.headline: IMD says Bay of Bengal depression may become a severe cyclonic storm
items.summary: The low over the southeast Bay became a depression on Nov 15; IMD forecasts a cyclonic storm on Nov 16 and a severe cyclonic storm on Nov 17. It would be the season's third cyclone and take the name Akvan.

items.headline: Nueces River warning raised to moderate flooding through Nov 18
items.summary: The river is forecast to crest near 16 ft, the moderate lowland flood threshold. The warning was upgraded from minor during the day and covers oil-field equipment along the floodplain.

items.headline: BoM warns severe thunderstorms are likely across eastern Australia
items.summary: The Bureau's severe weather update covers Nov 15 and 16 for eastern states.

items.headline: NASA says the 2026 El Niño could be bigger than the 1997-98 event
items.summary: NASA sea-level data show this El Niño strengthened more abruptly than 1997-98. The analysis does not say where the worst impacts will fall.

renewables.overview_html: The UK government refused the 840 MW Botley West solar farm, the first rejection of a solar project under the national infrastructure regime. In Germany, Envision and ju:niz added a 442 MWh grid-forming battery in Bavaria.

items.headline: UK refuses consent for the 840 MW Botley West solar farm
items.summary: The energy secretary rejected the Oxfordshire project on the inspectorate's advice; 69% of the site was Green Belt. PV Tech says it is the first refusal of a solar nationally significant infrastructure project.

items.headline: Envision and ju:niz plan a 442 MWh battery in Bavaria
items.summary: The Smareg 13 project at Vöhringen will use Envision's Gen 8 platform with four-hour duration and grid-forming inverters. Grid-forming storage helps stabilise frequency when wind and solar output swings.

science.overview_html: A thin week for new research. A preprint on WeatherDreamer trains one model to do both data assimilation and forecasting from 18 observing systems. A study using atmospheric oxygen measurements finds the ocean carbon sink is growing but its growth is slowing.

items.headline: WeatherDreamer learns assimilation and forecasting from 18 observing systems
items.summary: The world model ingests raw observations and produces an hourly global analysis in about 1.5 minutes on one GPU.

items.headline: Oxygen data show the ocean carbon sink growing more slowly
items.summary: The study uses paired atmospheric O2 and CO2 trends to split uptake between ocean and land. The ocean is absorbing more carbon than before, but the rate of increase is falling.

items.title: Spire Global wins a $33.2M NOAA task order starting Dec 1
items.body_html: NOAA awarded Spire a $33.2M task order for a two-year period beginning Dec 1, 2026. Spire also reported more than $70M in new weather awards and guided to about 30% growth in 2027.

items.title: Mercator Ocean joins EU Arctic observing project Beyond Arctic PASSION
items.body_html: Mercator Ocean International is a partner in the €8.5M Horizon Europe project, which links Arctic observing networks across more than 40 organisations over 48 months. Mercator handles data and Copernicus integration.
